image_description: A close-up, low-angle shot of a pedestrian traffic signal head. The housing is dark and curved with a large visor. Inside, an LED matrix displays a 'Walk' symbol (a walking person) composed of red, yellow, and green pixels, creating a gradient effect rather than distinct signal states. The background is dark and indistinct, possibly a building facade at night.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The 'walking person' icon is rendered with a pixelated LED grid that looks slightly irregular. The color transition from red (head) to yellow (torso) to green (legs) is physically unusual for a standard pedestrian signal (which is typically monochrome red or green/white). This suggests either a custom/artistic signal or an AI hallucination of how pedestrian signals work.

The curvature of the visor and the housing rim shows slight inconsistency in perspective lines. The left edge of the housing seems to warp slightly inward near the bottom, which may be lens distortion or minor geometric generation error.

The background is extremely dark and lacks detail, appearing as a smooth gradient rather than distinct architectural features. This could be intentional depth-of-field blur or AI smoothing of complex backgrounds.

Geometric integrity of the curved visor and housing
Edge sharpness against the dark background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'walking person' symbol. Standard pedestrian signals are usually monochrome (Red for Stop, Green/White for Walk). A simultaneous Red-Yellow-Green gradient on a single figure is highly suspicious and may indicate an AI misunderstanding of traffic signal logic. Evaluate if this is a rare artistic installation or a generation artifact. Also, scrutinize the housing geometry for subtle warping.
